summary: Ethiopia's official eVisa portal (evisa.gov.et) offers a 30-day single-entry tourist eVisa to citizens of all countries and lists the nationalities that can also get a tourist visa on arrival at Addis Ababa Bole airport; citizens of Kenya and Djibouti with a valid passport can enter without a visa.

payments.text: The UK Foreign Office describes Ethiopia as a cash-based society: card payments and ATMs are limited and unreliable, especially outside cities, so get enough cash before leaving them.

safety.text: The UK advises against all travel to the Tigray, Amhara and Gambela regions, to parts of Afar (within 20km of the Eritrean border and 50km of the Tigray boundary), Oromia, Somali and Benishangul-Gumuz, and to most land border areas, and against all but essential travel to the rest of Afar and Benishangul-Gumuz and to further parts of Oromia and Somali. It says all civilian flights to and from Tigray were suspended on 22 September 2026, that kidnapping is widespread in parts of the country, with incidents in the Oromia, Amhara and Somali regions, and that mugging is on the rise.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Ethiopia?
faq.answer: Yes, unless you are a citizen of Kenya or Djibouti: the Immigration and Citizenship Service says citizens of those two countries with a valid passport can enter without a visa. Everyone else can apply for the official tourist eVisa at evisa.gov.et, and some nationalities can also get a tourist visa on arrival at Addis Ababa Bole airport.

faq.question: How do I get the Ethiopian eVisa?
faq.answer: Apply online at evisa.gov.et with a passport scan and a photo. The single-entry tourist eVisa is issued for 30 days (USD 62), and the portal says processing normally takes 3 days.

faq.question: Can I get a visa on arrival in Ethiopia?
faq.answer: Yes, if your nationality is on the list. The Immigration and Citizenship Service lists the nationalities eligible for a tourist visa on arrival at Addis Ababa Bole International Airport, among them the US, UK, Canada, EU states, China and India; the full list is on evisa.gov.et under Tourist Visa (On Arrival). Every nationality can also apply for the eVisa online before travel.

faq.question: Is Ethiopia safe to visit?
faq.answer: Large parts of the country are off limits: the UK advises against all travel to the Tigray, Amhara and Gambela regions and to parts of Afar, Oromia and Somali. The Government of Canada says there are ongoing armed clashes between ethnic groups and with security forces in much of the country.

faq.question: Do I need a yellow fever vaccination for Ethiopia?
faq.answer: WHO lists Ethiopia as requiring a certificate only from travellers aged 9 months or over who arrive from a country with risk of yellow fever transmission.
